findings.title: Right-floated small-action button loses alignment in new flex container
findings.body: .small-action is made a flex container at lines 264-265, but its direct-child button still relies on float: right at line 309. Floats do not apply to flex items, and no margin-left: auto, justify-content, or equivalent replacement is added, so the button will sit immediately after .small-action-desc instead of at the right edge of the row.

findings.title: order() mistranslates flex order for legacy WebKit/Mozilla box layout
findings.body: The order() mixin copies the same value to order and to -webkit-box-ordinal-group/-moz-box-ordinal-group, but the legacy ordinal-group properties are 1-based and unordered items default to group 1, whereas flex order is 0-based and unordered items default to 0. Thus order(0) is invalid for legacy box layout and order(1) collides with unordered items there while following them in modern flex layout; the legacy properties need $val + 1 to preserve the same ordering.

findings.title: align-items() has incomplete and invalid legacy vendor mappings
findings.body: flexbox() and inline-flex() emit -moz-box/-moz-inline-box displays, but align-items() provides no -moz-box-align, so alignment is ignored by the legacy Mozilla box implementation for the header centering, .small-action centering, and bullet-badge baseline alignment. The block also emits the non-existent -ms-align-items property at line 121 while the actual IE10 property is -ms-flex-align, so that line is dead code and does not provide the intended support.

findings.title: extra-info-wrapper becomes a flex item without shrink/truncation constraints
findings.body: Adding order(2) makes .extra-info-wrapper participate as a flex item between the header title and the order(3) panel in the new .d-header .contents flex container, but it gets no flex sizing, min-width: 0, overflow, or truncation rules. A long topic title with category badges therefore cannot shrink below its content size and can push or compress the panel, causing the header controls to overflow or be clipped on narrow widths instead of the topic info truncating.
